papers.finding: The estimated probability of a Severe or Extreme event rose from 2.2% to 26.2% in Cluster 2, compared with 1.8% to 6.1% in Cluster 1 (cluster × period, p < 0.001).

papers.title: Water temperature and velocity alter mineral composition and iodine concentration in Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar)
papers.finding: These results demonstrate that elevated temperature can substantially alter the mineral composition of Atlantic salmon, with pronounced reductions in iodine concentrations.

papers.title: Snake River Sockeye Salmon Hatchery Program, ESA Section 10(a)(1)(A) (Reinitiation 2026)
Molecular Stress Biomarkers in Aquaculture: A Systematic Review
papers.finding: These studies evaluated molecular biomarkers of stress across 31 fish species, with Salmo salar being the most frequently studied, followed by Oncorhynchus mykiss.

papers.title: Turning Up the Heat: Why Tasmanian Atlantic Salmon Are in a League of Their Own
papers.finding: Rising ocean temperatures amplify both opportunity and risk: moderate warming will increase growth rates, whereas marine heatwaves and associated stressors can challenge fish health, welfare, and production stability.

papers.title: Defining Threshold Limits for Multiple Abiotic Stressors in Fisheries and Aquaculture Systems
papers.finding: These stressors, including temperature fluctuations, dissolved oxygen depletion, pH alterations, ammonia accumulation, salinity changes, excessive stocking density, and contamination by inorganic and organic pollutants, can adversely affect fish physiology, growth, reproduction, immunity, and survival.

papers.title: Climate change-related stressors in aquaculture: modulation of gill microbiota and transcriptome in Atlantic salmon
papers.finding: Overall, the results provide important evidence regarding how combined stressors may affect Atlantic salmon's gill mucosal health and highlight key genes and microbial taxa to be explored in more detail to understand the mechanisms behind climate-change effects on aquaculture.

papers.title: Hypoxia in Atlantic salmon aquaculture: Current understanding and the way forward toward mitigation and predictive management
papers.finding: We examine how low oxygen affects Atlantic salmon across biological scales, from respiratory and cardiovascular adjustments to metabolic reallocation, stress-axis activation, osmoregulatory disturbance, immune modulation, altered behavior, reduced appetite, impaired growth, disease susceptibility, mortality risk, and potential effects on product quality.

papers.title: Influence of Early Life Stage Hatchery Enhancement Practices on Maternal Reproductive Investment in Coho Salmon (Oncorhynchus kisutch)
papers.finding: I evaluated body size, fecundity, ovary weight, egg weight, egg volume, and proximate egg composition across groups while controlling for maternal body size and sampling year.

papers.title: Nutritional strategies to improve Atlantic salmon (salmo salar) liver health at suboptimal cold temperatures
papers.finding: Reducing total lipid by 20% while increasing EPA+DHA by 25% preserved liver fat content and membrane integrity at 2℃ by maintaining elevated levels of PL, ST, and LC-PUFA, as well as increasing expression of scdb and hsp70 transcripts.

papers.title: Epigenetics in Captivity: Restoring Wild Phenotypes in Captive‐Reared Salmonids
papers.finding: Ultimately, collaborative multi-disciplinary research across species is needed to understand the comprehensive effects of captive rearing, reduce the ecological impacts of captive fish in the wild, and increase population resilience.

papers.title: Aerobic scope is sustained through a heatwave in juvenile Atlantic salmon ( Salmo salar )
papers.finding: These findings suggest that juvenile Atlantic salmon may have limited capacity to increase aerobic performance during moderate heatwaves, leaving them vulnerable to cumulative effects of oxygen limitation to vital functions such as growth and stress responses.

papers.title: From heat stress to health collapse: A global review of temperature-mediated disease risk in fish
papers.journal: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
papers.finding: Documented case studies demonstrate that elevated temperatures frequently coincide with increased prevalence and severity of bacterial, parasitic, and fungal diseases, often amplified by concurrent stressors such as hypoxia, salinity fluctuations, poor water quality, and high stocking density.

papers.finding: In conclusion, big triploid Atlantic salmon were more vulnerable to environmental extremes driven by oxygen supply limitation and higher basal maintenance costs.

papers.title: Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid (GABA) as a Dietary Strategy for Enhancing Temperature Stress Resilience in Aquaculture Species
papers.finding: We not only spotlight GABA's role in the central nervous system, where it has been shown to modulate stress responses by enhancing antioxidant defenses, improving growth performance, and boosting disease resistance, but also emphasize the limited exploration of its potential to mitigate temperature stress in some aquaculture species, particularly economically important fish like olive flounder.
